IdempotencyKey.description: Required on every write. Same key + same request within 24 h replays the stored response.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

ApiApplicationResponse.description: The v1 wire format is snake_case, and deliberately not the merchant-dashboard shape: it answers "whose credentials are these, and where do their webhooks go".

ApiEventResponse.description: The v1 event: the SAME envelope a delivery's body carries, plus `object`.

has_unmatched_transfer.description: At least one transfer landed under one of this order's checkout sessions' references and could not be adopted as its payment — money the merchant may owe back.

interval.description: SUBSCRIPTION mode only. UPPERCASE: an output-only enum no request body carries.

mode.description:
`mode` and `ui_mode` round-trip on the published API (fix round 2, S5): they go in lowercase (`"payment"`, `"redirect"`) and they come back lowercase, from v1 responses AND from webhook payloads. An integrator can feed a session straight back into a create call.

STATUS fields deliberately stay UPPERCASE: they are output-only enums that no request body ever carries, so there is nothing for them to round-trip with. The payer-facing `checkout/session` view is an internal contract with our own checkout-frontend and is unchanged.

url.description: The hosted payment link. Returned ONLY by create and by reissuing the link: the token is never recoverable, so every other read returns null.

cancel_at.description: The EFFECTIVE end once `cancel_at_period_end` is true: the payer's own on-chain expiry when one was recorded, else `current_period_end` — never a raw column read (task-12 review I1; see `publishedCancelAt`). Null until a cancellation is scheduled, and always null once the subscription has ENDED, including an immediate cancel-now end, which clears the schedule entirely (I2).

anyOf.description: Who asked for a scheduled cancellation — the published `cancel_reason` / `cancelReason`. The same two values `end_reason` takes once the cancellation takes effect.

cancel_reason.description: WHO scheduled the cancellation `cancel_at` dates: `PAYER_CANCELED` (in their own wallet) or `MERCHANT_CANCELED` — the values `end_reason` takes once it ends. Null whenever `cancel_at` is null (nothing scheduled, or ENDED), and ALSO null for a scheduled cancel that recorded no reason (the ALERTed `no_reason` state — see `cancelReasonOf`), where `cancel_at` is non-null. Additive (final review parked #10; m5).

latest_payment.description: The newest payment of this subscription that SUCCEEDED — the last money that actually arrived (plan-2 re-review O2). Never an in-flight or failed attempt: those surface as `status: PAST_DUE` and the `subscription.payment_failed` webhook. `status` is kept for parity with the webhook `payment` object and always reads `SUCCEEDED`.

merchant_cancel_requested.description: True when the merchant ALSO asked to cancel at period end while the payer's own cancellation (`cancel_reason: PAYER_CANCELED`) was pending: it stands even if the payer resumes on chain. Additive (2026-09-28).

ApiTestEventResponse.description: `POST v1/webhook/test-event`'s 202 body: the id of the test.event queued for delivery.

EndpointVerificationPayload.description: The `endpoint.verification` probe's `data`: echo `challenge` back at HTTP 200.

code.description: Known codes are listed; treat any other string as an unknown error.

OrderEventPayload.description: The webhook body for order.paid / order.expired (spec §6.6, constraints.md's published payload table). Built from EXPLICIT keys, in the published order — never a spread of `toApiOrderResponse`, which also carries `description` and `canceled_at`: fields the published contract does not list. The contract wins; a dashboard-only field must not leak into a webhook just because the API response and the webhook payload happen to share most of their shape.

SessionEventPayload.description: The webhook body for the three checkout.session.* events (spec §6.6).

mode.description:
`mode` and `ui_mode` round-trip on the published API (fix round 2, S5): they go in lowercase (`"payment"`, `"redirect"`) and they come back lowercase, from v1 responses AND from webhook payloads. An integrator can feed a session straight back into a create call.

STATUS fields deliberately stay UPPERCASE: they are output-only enums that no request body ever carries, so there is nothing for them to round-trip with. The payer-facing `checkout/session` view is an internal contract with our own checkout-frontend and is unchanged.

SubscriptionEventPayload.description:
THE webhook payload, identical for all six subscription events (spec §6.6). Public ids only, amounts as base-unit strings, absent values null — never omitted, so an integrator can destructure it without optional chaining.

`payment` is REQUIRED, so every publisher has to decide which payment its event is about (final review I3): the settling payment for `created` / `renewed`, the failing SENT charge for `payment_failed` / `past_due` / `ended(PAYMENT_FAILED)` — or null when the failure was found before anything was sent — and null for `cancel_scheduled` and a cancel's `ended`. Null is published as `{ id: null, status: null, signature: null }`, never a missing key.

anyOf.description: Who asked for a scheduled cancellation — the published `cancel_reason` / `cancelReason`. The same two values `end_reason` takes once the cancellation takes effect.
